particular School, so as to verify how many students are
actually studying in the School and upto which class. The
District Education Officer with the aid of District Survey
Officer, shall also try to ascertain the area which can be
allotted to the Trust for the purpose of running this
particular School in consonance with Para 11 of our order
referred to above.
5. We direct the District Education Officer to file an
appropriate report before us as regards the aforesaid by
the next date of hearing.
6. Post the matter on 15th October, 2026.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.           OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO.13544/2026)
GANGA PRASAD BAIS      APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH & ANR.     RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned  counsel  for  the  respondent-State  of  Madhya
Pradesh.
3. By filing this appeal, appellant has assailed the
legality and correctness of the impugned order dated
22.04.2026 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at
Jabalpur (briefly ‘the High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting
the regular bail application of the appellant.
4. Appellant is an accused in FIR No.516/2025 registered
at Police Station- Chitrangi, District- Singrauli, Madhya
Pradesh under Sections 8, 21 and 22 of the Narcotics Drugs
and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (for short, ‘NDPS
Act’).
5. Allegation against the accused is that 41 bottles of
1

--- Page 356 ---
Onrex cough syrup were recovered from the joint possession
of the appellant and another co-accused, which is beyond
the commercial quantity.
6. Appellant is in custody since 05.12.2025.
7. This  Court  had  issued  notice  vide  order  dated
03.08.2026, pursuant to which learned counsel for the
respondent-State  of  Madhya  Pradesh  has  filed  counter
affidavit.
8. Learned  counsel  for  the  appellant  submits  that
appellant is a young person, aged 19 years at the time of
apprehension (now he would be 20 years of age). He has no
previous criminal antecedent. Referring to the FIR and the
deposition  of  the  02  independent  witnesses,  Sachin
Agrahari and Brijender Sain, before the Court, he submits
that the 02 independent witnesses have totally disowned
whatever has been attributed to them by the police. In
fact,  they  have  stated  that  they  had  not  seen  the
appellant and were not present at the place where the
seizure was made or when the appellant was apprehended.
Being a young person without any criminal antecedent,
appellant deserves to be treated leniently and, therefore,
should be granted bail.
9. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent-State
of Madhya Pradesh submits that total quantity of the
contraband seized would be 04 litres, which is well beyond
the  commercial  quantity.  Not  only  investigation  is
complete, the trial has commenced. Out of 11 prosecution
2

--- Page 357 ---
witnesses, 03 have been examined. Therefore, this Court
may consider directing the Trial Court to expedite the
trial instead of considering bail of the appellant.
10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on
going through the materials on record, we are of the view
that a case for bail is made out.
11. That being the position, t he impugned order dated
22.04.2026 passed by the High Court is set aside.
12. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall be
produced before the jurisdictional Special Court within a
maximum period of 07 days from today, whereafter he shall
be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be
deemed appropriate.
13. Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
14. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

   [UJJAL BHUYAN]
…………………………………………………...J.
     [ATUL S. CHANDURKAR]
NEW DELHI;
16th SEPTEMBER, 2026.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL  NO(S).  6083/2024
  R. SAKUNTALA (DEAD) THR. LRS.                     APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
HAJI KHATIJA BEEVI TRUST NAGAPATINAM & ORS.        RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. The main matter itself has been taken up for hearing today. 
2. With respect to the controversy on the case at hand i.e., the
retrospective application of the procedural amendment in the
Wakf (Amendment) Act, 2013, the law has been quite settled by
a decision of this Court in ‘Mumtaz Yarud Dowla Wakf Vs. M/s
Badam Balakrishna Hotel Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.’ , reported in (2023)
SCC OnLine SC 1378. Even on merits, we do not find anything in
favour of the appellant. In fact, the present appeal itself is
not maintainable, as it has been filed in the name of a dead
person. 
3. Before the High Court, it was contested by the deceased R.
Sakuntala who died on 12.04.2021. However, the present appeal
has been filed on 08.05.2021 in her own name, as if she was
alive. Thereafter, the applications for substitution, for

--- Page 360 ---
2
condonation of delay, and for setting aside abatement have
been filed. 
4. In such view of the matter, the appeal stands dismissed; and
the applications for condonation of delay in filing the
application for setting aside the abatement, for setting aside
abatement,  and  for  substitution  are  allowed.  The  legal
representatives of the appellants are duly taken on record.
5. While dismissing the appeal, we take into the consideration
the fact that the appellants (legal representatives) have been
in possession for quite a long period of time. In such view of
the matter, we grant four months from the date of receipt of a
copy of this order for the appellants to handover the vacant
possession to the respondent, subject to the undertaking that
they  shall  vacate  it  on  or  before  the  date  so  fixed.
Additionally, they shall pay the admitted rent, including the
arrears. The undertaking be filed within two weeks.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

T.P.(C) No. 1476/2025
O R D E R
1. These matters were taken up for further hearing today.
2. The petitioner, Dr. Pratibha Mayur Thakkar and the respondent,
Dr. Mayur Deepak Thakkar have joined the proceedings online.
3. Prima facie,  we are of the view that the present case is now
one of an irretrievable breakdown of marriage.
4. We  tried  our  best  to  persuade  the  parties  to  save  the
marriage, at least keeping in mind the interest of their minor
son, Pransh, who is four years of age but, unfortunately, our
efforts did not yield any positive result.
5. In such circumstances, the two transfer petitions at the
instance of the wife, i.e., T.P. (C) No.2066/2025 and T.P.
(Crl.)  No.707/2025, respectively,  are allowed  whereas the
transfer petition preferred by the husband i.e., T.P. (C)
No.1476/2025 is dismissed. 
1

--- Page 376 ---
6. Consequently, the Divorce Petition bearing Petition A No.3169
of 2024 titled as “ Dr. Mayur Deepak Thakkar vs. Dr. Pratibha
Mayur  Thakkar ”, pending before the Family Court at Bandra,
Mumbai and the Domestic Violence case bearing No. PWDVA CASE
DV/6/2025 titled as “Mrs. Asha Deepak Thakkar vs. Dr. Pratibha
Mayur  Thakkar ”, pending before the 27 th Judicial Magistrate
First Class at Mulund, Mumbai are ordered to be transferred to
the Family Court, Raipur, Chhattisgarh.
7. The transferor courts shall forthwith transmit the records of
the aforesaid cases to the transferee court.
8. The transferee court shall make all possible endeavours first
for an amicable settlement between the parties, failing which
for  early  decision  in  the  matter(s)  without  unnecessary
adjournments.
9. The respondent-husband shall appear in all the proceedings
online before the transferee court, except on such date(s)
when his personal presence is mandatorily required by the
Court.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Criminal Appeal Nos.4374-4375 of 2026
[ @ Special Leave Petition (Crl.) Nos.972-973 of 2026 ]
Sivabalan and Anr.
       ...Appellants
Versus
The Union Territory of Puducherry & Anr.
           ...Respondents
O R D E R
Leave granted.
2. The appellants are the accused and the second respondent is a
complainant,  at  whose  instance  an  FIR  was  registered  as  Crime
No.158 of 2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 294(b),
323, 34, 506(ii) of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and Sections 3(1)(r)
and  3(1)(s)  of  the  Scheduled  Castes  and  Scheduled  Tribes
(Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (SC/ST Act) at Mudaliarpet Police
Station, District Puducherry. The petitioner in the application filed
before the High Court sought for quashing of the FIR, which was
declined by the High Court by the impugned order.
3. We heard Sri Shyam Gopal, learned Counsel appearing for the
1

--- Page 400 ---
appellants, Sri. Aravindh S., learned Advocate-on-Record appearing
for State and Sri. Abhisar Thakral, learned Counsel appearing for the
second respondent.
4. The  records  indicate  various  cases  pending  between  the
parties, however, we are only concerned with the quashing of the
instant  FIR  bearing  Crime  No.158  of  2023.  The  first  appellant  is
carrying on business and so is the second respondent; despite, the
second respondent being an Advocate. In fact, we see notices having
been issued on his behalf styling himself as a proprietor of one M/s
United Power System, which however, is not the subject matter of
this case. The allegation in the FIR was that on 09.11.2022, the
second  respondent  was  called  by  the  appellants  to  a  Hotel  for
settlement of certain disputes in the business transactions between
the two parties. It is the specific case in Annexure P23 that he was
called to a Hotel where he was invited into a room inside which he is
said to have been attacked and abused with casteist slurs.
5. Pertinent is the fact      that  the  second  respondent  had  filed
a  similar  complaint,  making  the  very  same
allegations earlier.The said complaint was withdrawn as per Annexure
P18.  Even  earlier  Annexure  P12  complaint  was  filed,  which  was
withdrawn as per Annexure P15. Multiple complaints have been filed
2

--- Page 401 ---
under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and
the disputes are with respect to business and financial transactions;
as is evident from the records. The allegation under SC/ST Act is an
afterthought, and in any event the accusation is that such casteist
slurs were made in a room and not attracting the specific provisions
alleged.
6. We  find  absolutely  no  reason  to  permit  the  second
respondent’s FIR filed as Crime No.158 of 2023 to continue and we
quash the same as against the appellants herein.
7. The appeals are disposed of.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand rejected.
.......…….……………………. J.
              (J. B. PARDIWALA)
....……….……………………. J.
                                      (K. VINOD CHANDRAN)
NEW DELHI;
SEPTEMBER 15, 2026.

monthly maintenance of Rs.8,000/- (Rupees eight thousand)
to  the  first  respondent  and  Rs.6,000/-  (Rupees  six
thousand) each to respondent Nos. 2 and 3/two sons born
1

--- Page 408 ---
from  the wedlock.   The  petitioner has  no grievance
against  the  maintenance  awarded  to  the  two  sons  @
Rs.6,000/- (Rupees six thousand) each from the date of
filing  of  the  application.  Learned  counsel  for  the
petitioner submits that the entire arrears have been paid
and the children are being paid the maintenance.  
3. The  grievance  of  the  petitioner  is  that  the
petitioner has obtained proof that after passing of the
impugned order to the effect that the first respondent is
remarried.
4. Learned  counsel  draws  attention  to  ‘Obituary’
column published in ‘Mathrubhumi’ newspaper.  Learned
counsel has furnished appropriate translation.  According
to  learned  counsel,  the  respondent  No.1/Jeesha  P  is
married to one Sri T.Vijesh. Learned counsel contends
that in view this remarriage, respondent No.1 is not
entitled to claim maintenance from the petitioner.
5. Since it is a change in circumstance, we are of the
opinion that the petitioner should be allowed to pursue
such other remedies, as are available to him in law.
Respondent No.1 has chosen not to appear, in spite of
service.  Hence, we are inclined to dispose of the
present  Special  Leave  Petition  by  permitting  the
petitioner to raise this ground which is being brought to
our notice before the appropriate forum/Court.
2

--- Page 409 ---
6. Since respondent No.1 is not appearing before us to
traverse  this  fact,  we  keep  the  order  awarding
maintenance of Rs.8,000/- (Rupees eight thousand) to her
in abeyance for a period of three weeks. 
7. Within  the  said  period  of  three  weeks,  the
petitioner shall avail such other remedy as are available
to him in law.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner before this Court has filed this present
petition being aggrieved by Order dated 15.04.2025 passed by the
Madurai Bench of Madras High Court in Crl. R.C. (MD). No. 104 of
1

--- Page 441 ---
2025.
2. The facts of the case reveal that the petition was preferred
by the petitioner under 497 of BNSS to return the vehicle bearing
Registration No. TN 75 AD 1353 which was seized in respect of Crime
No. 182/2024 under Section 272 of Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)
2023. The petitioner being the registered owner of the vehicle
submitted an application for return of the vehicle and the same was
rejected by the Trial Court and this those circumstances the
Criminal Revision was preferred before the High Court and the High
Court has also dismissed the application vide impugned order dated
15.04.2025. Learned counsel for the petitioner stated before this
Court that the vehicle in question is an old vehicle and since 2024
it is lying outside the police station and everyday the condition
of the vehicle is deteriorating, the spare parts are missing and
nothing will be left by the time the trial is concluded. She has
stated that the vehicle be released on terms and conditions as
framed by this Court.
3. On the other hand learned counsel for the State of Tamil Nadu
has vehemently opposed the prayer for release of the vehicle in
question and he has stated that people from the neighboring State
are  dumping  garbage  in  State  of  Tamil  Nadu  and  in  those
circumstances the question of release of vehicle does not arise.
4. This Court without averting to the main controversy involved
in the present case is of the opinion that the vehicle deserves to
be released as its value is depreciating everyday and it is parked
in an open space. The interest of justice be subserved in case the
2

--- Page 442 ---
vehicle is released subject to deposit of Rs.1,00,000/- before the
Court of Judicial Magistrate No.1, Kuzhithurai, where the case is
pending. Let the same be deposited within three weeks and the
vehicle in question shall be released within one week thereafter.
5. It is also made clear that the petitioner will not dispose of
the vehicle till Cr. No. 182/2024 is concluded and the Trial Court
shall be free to pass appropriate order based upon the outcome of
the criminal case.
6. With the aforesaid observation, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of.
7. Pending application(s), if any shall also stand disposed.
(PRIYANKA MALIK)                                  (KOMAL)

SLP(C) No. 20302/2024
1. The present petition is arising out of interim order dated

2023. The High Court of Delhi has granted interim order thereby
directing 50% of the awarded amount alongwith interest in the
matter. Learned counsel for the petitioner arguing before this
Court that as per Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 a sum of
Rs.25,000/- or 50% whichever is less is required to be deposited in
the matter.
2. In the present case the accident is of the year 2014 and the
child in question has suffered 100% disability and the family is
badly in need of the money.
3. Service is complete on claimant/respondent No.1, but none has
entered appearance.
4. Keeping in view the totality of the circumstance of the case,
we hereby modify the order passed by the High Court directing the
petitioner to pay a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- within a period of 30
days from today. The money so deposited shall be released in favour
of the claimant(s).
5. With the above observation, the Special Leave Petition shall
stand disposed of with the request to the High Court of Delhi to
decide the matter on merits in accordance with law.
6. Question of law is kept open.
7. Pending application(s), if any shall also stand disposed of.

ITEM NO.8               COURT NO.1               SECTION X
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Writ Petition(s)(Criminal)  No(s).  275/2026
RAVI KUMAR                                         Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
L. NARSIMHA REDDY & ORS.                           Respondent(s)
(IA No. 210808/2026 - PERMISSION TO APPEAR AND ARGUE IN PERSON)
 
Date : 17-09-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) :  Petitioner-in-person
                    
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Permission to appear and argue in person is granted.
2. This  Writ  Petition  has  been  filed  relying  upon  various
provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 read with Article
32 of the Constitution, seeking a direction for the registration of
an FIR against respondent Nos.1 and 2, who are the former Chairman
of  the  Central  Administrative  Tribunal  (CAT)  and  former
Administrative Member of CAT, respectively.  The aforesaid prayer
is  founded  upon  the  allegation  that  there  was  forgery  and
fabrication of the judicial record.
3. The petitioner is a practising advocate.  He was appointed as
a Consultant (Administration) in the International Solar Alliance
(ISA)  under  the  Ministry  of  New  and  Renewable  Energy.  His
1

--- Page 462 ---
engagement was, however, terminated, which prompted him to approach
the CAT through O.A. No.1669/2017. It seems that the O.A. was
dismissed, and some derogatory, highly objectionable and uncalled-
for expressions used by the petitioner led to the initiation of the
contempt proceedings, in which he was held guilty. The petitioner
was granted time to tender an unconditional apology, but that was
also found unsatisfactory, and the sentence of 30 days awarded to
him was confirmed.
4. From the paper book, we do not find any material to suggest
that the aforesaid order holding the petitioner guilty of contempt
was ever challenged before a superior forum or that the order was
set aside.  
5. The  petitioner,  however,  claims  that  he  tendered  an
unconditional apology on 20.12.2018.   Although the paper book does
not  disclose  this,  it  seems  that  a  Criminal  Appeal  (Diary)
No.4239/2019 was filed before this Court, which was, however,
withdrawn by the petitioner’s counsel on 11.02.2019.
6. Be that as it may, after seven years, the petitioner in person
has chosen to file this petition, making highly scandalous and
defamatory allegations against the members of the CAT and the High
Court judges. We do not expect a person who claims himself to be a
practising lawyer to indulge in this kind of arm-twisting and
browbeating of the CAT or the High Court. The appropriate recourse
for the petitioner would have been to avail of the remedy in
accordance with the law. It seems that such a remedy was availed,
though it was not disclosed in the instant proceedings. All that we
wish to observe is that the instant Writ Petition is totally
2

--- Page 463 ---
frivolous and scandalous. The same is, accordingly, dismissed.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.
(NITIN TALREJA)                            (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        DY. REGISTRAR

--- Page 492 ---
Yadav  &  Ors. "  pending  before  Court  of  Metropolitan
Magistrate,  Saidapet,  Chennai  and  Complaint  Case  STC
No.126/2024 titled as " Samunnati  Financial  Intermediation
and  Services  Private  Limited  vs.  Kajal  Yadav " pending
before  the  Court  of  Judicial  Magistrate  (Fast  Track
Court),  Tiruvannamalai  to  the  Court  of  competent
jurisdiction at Katni, District Katni, Madhya Pradesh.
3. Mr. Ashutosh Dubey, learned counsel appearing for
the petitioner submits that the Courts at Metropolitan
Magistrate,  Saidapet,  Chennai  and  (Fast  Track  Court),
Tiruvannamalai have no jurisdiction inasmuch no cause of
action arose within the territorial jurisdiction of these
Courts.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits
that the petitioner being an old lady is unable to join

ground urged on behalf of the petitioner that the Courts
at Metropolitan Magistrate, Saidapet, Chennai and (Fast
Track Court), Tiruvannamalai have no jurisdiction is not a
reason for transfer of a criminal case from one place to
another not at all be an issue to be decided in an
appropriate proceeding. The petitioner being an old lady
is also not a ground to transfer the criminal case.
6. This court does not find any reason to entertain
this petition. Accordingly, the transfer petition stands
dismissed.

1

--- Page 510 ---
not inclined to entertain these Special Leave Petition(s)
on merits, in view of the fact that the petitioner’s
earlier Special Leave Petition (C) No. 15763 of 2022 was
dismissed with liberty to apply to the High Court by
seeking review of the impugned order, however, no further
liberty was reserved to maintain a fresh Special Leave
Petition again after the order in review is passed by the
High Court. This Court has taken such view in the matter of
Kangra Central Cooperative Bank Limited vs. Kangra Central
Cooperative Bank Pensioners Welfare Association (Regd.) and
Ors.1,1. 
3. Despite the above, it is noticed that respondent
No.4 – School had given an affidavit / undertaking to the
Education Director, Directorate of Education, Lucknow on
04.10.2004, stating that even if the teachers (including
the  petitioner)  are  not  taken  on  grant  list  by  the
Government, then the School or the Managing Committee will
bear the expenses, from its own sources.
4. On 01.09.2026, we had directed respondent No.4 to
file an affidavit of compliance of the above aspect before
the next date of hearing. An affidavit has been filed by
respondent No.4, stating that the petitioner shall be taken
back on duty in the same status as he was on the date when
the  impugned  order  was  passed  by  the  High  Court  on
05.05.2022.
5. The Special Leave Petition(s) are dismissed, subject
1 . 2025 SCC OnLine SC 2771 
2

--- Page 511 ---

respondent No.4.

Crl.A. No. 4211/2025
1. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/applicant
and on perusal of the records as well as the post-mortem report, it clearly
indicates that the role attributed to the present appellant/applicant is that he
had assaulted the deceased on the right side of the neck by use of lathi.
Whereas A1 and A2 are said to have inflicted injuries on the head and other
parts of the body of the deceased by use of axe and spear and the cause of
death has been due to shock and haemorrhage. The appellant/applicant was on
bail during the entire period of trial as well as during the pendency of the appeal
before the High Court and had not violated the conditions imposed.  Hence, we
are of the considered view that the appellant/applicant is entitled for grant of
bail. 
2. Accordingly, Interlocutory Application No. 173581/2026 for grant of bail is
allowed.  Appellant/applicant  is  ordered  to  be  released  on  bail  by  the
jurisdictional Court on such terms and conditions as it may deem fit to impose.

--- Page 666 ---
2
for the State.
2. The appeals are already admitted.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the
appellant has already undergone about 24 years of actual
imprisonment. Learned counsel also submits that going by
the compliance report of the District & Sessions Judge,
Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh and counting date of birth
as 15.10.1985, the appellant will be juvenile on the
date of the offence.
4. Keeping all these factors in mind,  we are inclined
to suspend the sentence of the appellant and enlarge the
appellant on bail.
5. Accordingly, we suspend the sentence of appellant-
Indrajit Mallah and enlarge him on bail subject to the
satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court in connection
with Sessions Trial Nos.519/2002 and 520/2002 for the
offence punishable under Sections 364A & 201 of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Section 4/25 of the
Arms Act, 1959.
6. IA No. 40575/2023 is disposed of in the above terms.
7. List these appeals in the 3 rd week of January, 2027
subject to orders of Hon’ble the Chief Justice of India.

                                VERSUS
LAAD PRANAY SANJAY                                 Respondent(s)

For Petitioner(s) :Petitioner-in-person
                    
For Respondent(s) :Mr. Aayush B. Paranjpe, Adv.
                   Ms. Mantika Haryani, AOR
                   Mr. Bilal Ali, Adv.
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. This Transfer Petition was listed on 28.07.2026 before this
Court in which the following order was passed:-
“Application seeking permission to appear and argue in person
is allowed.
2. Issue notice, returnable within four weeks.
3. Till further orders, there shall be a stay of proceedings
in  Divorce  Petition  bearing  Matrimonial  Case  No.
HMA/5292/2025, titled as “Major Laad Pranay Sanjay vs. Sonali
Singh Rathore”, pending before the Court of the Principal
Judge, Family Court, Faridabad, Haryana.”
2. The respondent has been served and has entered appearance on
01.09.2026 and today, he represents that on 28.07.026  itself at
around 03.00 pm, HMA No. 5292/2025 was taken up and the respondent
was proceeded ex  parte. The case is now listed on 12.10.2026 for
recording the ex parte evidence of the petitioner.
3. The petitioner-in-person submits that she is not in a position
to appear before the Family Court in Faridabad and on 12.03.2026,
she had already made a request while appearing in person.

--- Page 1098 ---
4. Today confronted with this situation, the petitioner-in-person
submits that she had not engaged any lawyer before the Family
Court, Faridabad and therefore, she could not represent her case on
28.07.2026 on which date, her case was also listed in the Supreme
Court of India.
5. There seems to be a small communication error about the stay
order passed by this Court. Since it could not be communicated by
03.00 PM on the same day to the Family Court, Faridabad. The
respondent who appears through his advocate fairly submits that
they have no objection to the Transfer Petition being allowed.
Since there is an order by which the respondent has been set ex
parte,  that order may have to be recalled so as to enable the
transfer to get effected.  
6. In the interest of justice, we permit the petitioner to make
such an application before the Family Court, Faridabad to recall
the order dated 28.07.2026 setting her ex parte within a period of
one week from today. 
7. The  respondent  submits  that  he  will  be  appearing  and
cooperating for the said application being heard and disposed of
within a period of two weeks from today. List the Transfer Petition
after two weeks so as to enable this Court to pass an order in the
main Transfer Petition.
8. We  direct  the  Family  Court,  Faridabad  to  take  up  the
application immediately as soon as it is filed and dispose of the
same within a period of two weeks from today.
9. The petitioner may be permitted to appear virtually for moving
the said application.
10. List after two weeks.
(KANIKA TAYAL)                                  (POOJA KOHLI)

of receipt of copy of this order.

For Respondent(s) : 
                   Mr. Karan Sharma, AOR
                   Mr. Rajat Jain, Adv.                   
         UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Counter affidavit filed by the State of Punjab discloses that
nine criminal cases are registered against the petitioner and two
are still pending trial.
However, the petitioner disclosed the pendency of only one
case in the synopsis without mentioning the details thereof.
This is not in keeping with the law laid down by this Court in
“Munnesh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh” 1.  The special leave petition
is liable to be rejected on that short ground alone.  The same is,
accordingly, dismissed.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
